interface.title: Agronaut
interface.field: Aquaponics / hydroponics system engineering and field irrigation agronomy
interface.stage_of_work: Planning and design before building, then keeping farm records and running saved engineering calculations during a crop season
interface.what_it_is_for: Sizes an aquaponic system from species, crop, area, temperature and water budget, searches for the best fish-to-crop ratio, and runs cited field-irrigation and nutrient calculations that are saved against a farm's production unit and crop cycle, all with deterministic code.

data.note: The Design page uses built-in, cited coefficient tables and needs no data. Field records was given the test files field_water.json, drip_design.json and nutrient_budget.json. Only drip_design.json computed and saved. The other two were rejected with 'calculation timezone must match the farm timezone' because the farm was created with timezone Africa/Accra. According to the reviewer, who read the repo's example files, field_water.json sets Europe/Brussels and nutrient_budget.json sets UTC.

features.name: Constraint-driven system sizing form with headline metrics
features.general: Fill a short form of design inputs (organism, crops, area, temperature, resource budget, construction method), press one button, and get a feasibility verdict, condition warnings and a row of key sizes
features.specific: Size a system: fish species, crops multiselect, grow area, mean water temp, water budget, growing method → Size system → Feasible design, temperature-band warning when inputs fall outside the species' band, Feed/Fish/Biomass/System volume/Pump/Makeup water
steps: pick species and one or more crops
set area, temperature and water budget
pick growing method (raft / nft / media_bed / vertical_tower)
press Size system
read the verdict, the warnings and the metric tiles
serves_tasks: Enter the organism, crops, area, temperature and water budget, and get component sizes
Re-run the sizing with a different construction method and condition

features.name: Parametric system schematic with SVG export
features.general: A flow diagram of the designed system that redraws from the computed sizes and can be downloaded as a vector file; downloading clears the computed design, so it must be recomputed afterwards
features.specific: System schematic: rearing tank → biofilter → grow beds → sump + pump, labelled with fish count, volumes, media area, pump flow/head/watts; Download schematic (SVG) → agronaut_schematic.svg; pressing it clears the sized results back to 'Set your inputs and press Size system'
steps: size a system
read the boxes and flows labelled with computed values
change the method and see the bed type and volumes redraw
press Download schematic (SVG)
press Size system again to bring the results back
serves_tasks: Enter the organism, crops, area, temperature and water budget, and get component sizes
Export the design as a report and a diagram

features.name: Parts list and operating envelope
features.general: Fold-out sections under a computed design listing the components to buy at their computed sizes and the target and never-outside bands for each water-quality variable
features.specific: Bill of materials (rearing tank, grow beds, pump flow/head/watts, biofilter media area, aeration, fingerlings) and Operating envelope (pH, temperature, DO, ammonia/nitrite target and never-outside bands)
steps: size a system
open Bill of materials and read each component's size
open Operating envelope for the target and never-outside bands
serves_tasks: Review the parts list and the operating range to keep

features.name: Design cross-check against field data and a mass balance
features.general: Compare the design's operating range with a large public dataset of real measurements, and check the sizing with an independent mass balance that should agree with it
features.specific: Reality check — your envelope vs. real ponds (~232,745 readings, Udanor et al. 2022; real-pond medians flagged against your targets) and Nitrogen consistency check (N fed/kept/plants/solids/exchange/denitrification; supported vs. designed grow area and % apart)
steps: size a system
open Reality check to see where real ponds' medians fall against your targets
open Nitrogen consistency check and compare the area the nitrogen supports with the designed area
serves_tasks: Cross-check the design against real-world data and an independent mass balance

features.name: Design provenance: stated limits and cited coefficients
features.general: A list of what the method leaves out and a table of every coefficient with its value, range, unit and source, plus a verdict on whether the built-in value sits inside the published range
features.specific: What is NOT modeled (8 items: pH/alkalinity, non-N nutrients, P/K, salinity, solids/biofilter maturation, pests, cohort logic, diel temperature) and Coefficients used (cited) with FAO589/UVI/LIT sources and seed-vs-published range verdicts
steps: size a system
open What is NOT modeled
open Coefficients used (cited) to trace each number to its source and range verdict
serves_tasks: Read the method's stated limits and the cited source of each coefficient

features.name: Design report export with sensitivity table
features.general: Download a self-contained Markdown report of the design that adds a one-at-a-time sensitivity table (±20% on each input, plus the optimizer's best mix); downloading clears the computed design, so it must be recomputed afterwards
features.specific: Download design report (Markdown) → aquaponics-design-<site>.md with inputs, sized system, sensitivity, warnings, BOM, envelope, maintenance checklist, N check, assumptions, NOT modeled, coefficients; pressing it clears the sized results back to 'Set your inputs and press Size system'
steps: size a system with an optional site name
press Download design report (Markdown)
open the file to read the sensitivity rows and the checklist
press Size system again to bring the results back
serves_tasks: Export the design as a report and a diagram

features.name: Exhaustive mix optimizer with selectable objective and ranked alternatives
features.general: Choose an objective, narrow the candidate species and crops, and search every combination and mix proportion for the best one; see its gain over an even split, the runners-up and what the search ignores
features.specific: Find the best ratio: Maximize (Total food / Total protein / Water efficiency), Fish to consider and Crops to consider multiselects, Optimize → Best ratio banner, '+x% vs even split', Food/Protein/Makeup water, 'Searched N combinations', Top alternatives table, What is NOT optimized, Assumptions
steps: set area, temperature and water budget
pick the objective in Maximize
clear or narrow the fish and crop candidate lists
press Optimize and wait (up to about a minute for the full search)
open Top alternatives to compare near-best mixes
serves_tasks: Maximize total output across all candidate combinations
Restrict the candidate set and optimize a resource-efficiency objective
Compare runner-up solutions and read what the optimizer ignores

features.name: Site → season record scaffold
features.general: Register a site with management type and timezone, then add a dated planting with a provenance note so later records and calculations attach to that season
features.specific: Sidebar Add a production unit (production system, farm, water strategy, irrigation method, timezone, environment) → Create and use unit; Crop records > Record a planting (crop, date picker, record source) → Save planting → Crop cycle selector
steps: open Add a production unit and choose system and water strategy
name the unit and farm and set the timezone (it must match the timezone in calculation files you will save)
press Create and use unit
in Crop records open Record a planting, enter crop, pick a date, give a source
press Save planting and select the new cycle
serves_tasks: Register a site with its management type and local timezone
Start a growing season record for the site

features.name: Typed calculation import with saved, sourced result
features.general: Pick a calculation type, upload its JSON input, compute and save it against the selected season; the saved result shows the verdict, binding constraints, quantities, assumptions, limits and sources, and can be chosen again from a list
features.specific: Field records > Import and save a calculation: Calculation dropdown (16 types, e.g. Soil-water budget, Crop-water demand, drip/sprinkler hydraulics, Drip/Sprinkler equipment design, Mineral nutrient accounting) + JSON upload → Calculate and save → Saved calculation selector with the EXPERIMENTAL report
steps: select the crop cycle
choose the calculation type
upload the input JSON
press Calculate and save (in the run, files whose timezone differed from the farm's were rejected with 'calculation timezone must match the farm timezone')
pick it in Saved calculation and read its constraints, materials, limits and sources
serves_tasks: Upload a calculation input file, compute it and save the cited result to the season
